title: LinkedIn API Pricing 2026: Is It Free, and What Does It Cost?
snippet:
LinkedIn API pricing in 2026: the API has no fee, access is gated by product approval instead. What each product unlocks, Development vs Standard tier limits, what one post costs in API calls, the upload-then-post flow with Node and Python code, 60-day tokens, versioning, and the partner programs and scrapers that do cost money.

**TLDR:** The LinkedIn API is free. LinkedIn charges nothing per call and has no paid tier; what you pay instead is access. Personal-profile posting is self-serve, but company pages need Community Management API approval, a Development tier capped at 500 calls per app and 100 per member a day, and a screencast review to leave it. An image post is two API calls plus an upload, tokens expire every 60 days, and the API version must be bumped yearly. The only “LinkedIn APIs” that cost money are scrapers, and LinkedIn sues those. Checked against LinkedIn’s documentation on September 24, 2026.

> “The APIs are currently provided for free, but LinkedIn reserves the right to charge for the APIs in the future.”
The same section adds that if a fee is introduced you are not obliged to keep using the APIs. So the honest answer to “LinkedIn API pricing” is that there is no price list. There is no free tier and paid tier, no per-call metering, no key you buy. The only money that moves through a LinkedIn API is ad spend on the Advertising API, and that pays for ads, not calls. This is different from X, which charges per post and per read since February 2026 and whose rates we broke down in the [X API pricing guide](https://postzen.dev/blog/twitter-api-pricing), and different from the paid data APIs that Google will happily show you when you search this phrase.

| Route | Fee | Prerequisites | Review | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Share on LinkedIn (personal posting) | None | An app, a LinkedIn Page to associate it with, a privacy policy URL | None | 150 requests per member and 100,000 per app per day, per the Share on LinkedIn page |
| Community Management API, Development tier | None | Registered legal organization, business email, verified organization and domain, Page super admin verifies the app | Vetting of the business and use case | 500 calls per app and 100 per member per 24 hours; no batch calls; no webhooks; 12 months to finish building |
| Community Management API, Standard tier | None | All of the above plus a finished integration | Screencast of each declared use case, test credentials, data storage compliance | No restrictions

title: LinkedIn API Pricing: Complete Guide for 2026
snippet:
Two pieces of the **LinkedIn API**, LinkedIn’s set of OAuth 2.0 developer products, are open permissions any developer can switch on without approval: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, and Share on LinkedIn, which lets a member post, comment and like as themselves through `w_member_social`. A few others, like the Verified on LinkedIn Development tier, are self-serve on request. The ones most products need, posting to Company Pages through the Community Management API and running ads through the Advertising API (the Marketing Developer Platform, or MDP, in LinkedIn’s own token docs and in most guides), wait on LinkedIn’s approval, and LinkedIn lists no dollar price for any of its API products.
**How much does the LinkedIn API cost in 2026?** No API product carries a published fee. For the approval-gated products, the real cost is an approval cycle measured in months, not a monthly fee.

LinkedIn’s own [API Terms of Use](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/l/api-terms-of-use) put it in one line: “The APIs are currently provided for free, but LinkedIn reserves the right to charge for the APIs in the future.” The $699/month figure you’ll see quoted around the web is a third-party estimate, not a LinkedIn price. The table below shows both: what LinkedIn publishes, and what the estimates say.

| Access tier | Official cost (LinkedIn) | Third-party estimate | Best for | Key friction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consumer (Sign In with LinkedIn) | Free | $0 (no estimate needed) | Auth flows, basic profile, share to own feed | Tiny scopes, no analytics, no pages |
| Marketing Developer Platform | Not publicly priced. Partner-gated. | $699+/month, per [Phyllo](https://www.getphyllo.com/post/how-much-does-the-linkedin-api-cost-iv). Labeled an estimate by Phyllo itself, with no methodology published. | Pages, ads, scheduling on behalf of clients | Partner approval required, no published timeline (builders report weeks to months) |
|

| Verified on LinkedIn API | Development: Free, 5,000 calls/day. Lite: Free, 5,000 calls/day. Plus: Contact for custom pricing. | None published for Plus | Trust signals for marketplaces, freelance, communities | Access flow differs per tier (self-serve, app review, BD approval) |

Access to **Audience Insights** and **Media Planning** APIs is restricted to developers who meet additional qualification criteria evaluated by LinkedIn. The **Company Intelligence API** is not currently accepting new applications.

title: LinkedIn Pricing & API Plans | APIs.io
snippet:
LinkedIn does not charge per-call for its public APIs. Access is gated by program approval rather than tiered pricing. Consumer-facing products (Sign In, Share, Verified) are free. Marketing, Talent, Sales Navigator, Learning, and Compliance APIs are gated through partner programs and access tiers (Development, Standard, Enterprise) — what costs money is the underlying LinkedIn product (ad spend, Recruiter / Sales Navigator / Learning seats), not the API itself.

It defines 8 plans, covering freemium and enterprise tiers, with named plans including *Consumer APIs (Sign In / Share / Verified)*, *Marketing API — Development Tier*, *Marketing API — Standard Tier*, *Talent Solutions APIs (Recruiter System Connect / Job Posting)*, *Sales Navigator APIs (CRM Sync / Display / Analytics)*, and 3 more.

Consumer APIs (Sign In / Share / Verified) freemium
Free developer access to Sign In with LinkedIn, Share on LinkedIn, and Verified on LinkedIn. No charge per call; subject to LinkedIn API Terms of Use.
